# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer and mail carrier  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer is low in stature, heavy-set, and lacking hair. He has a circular countenance and bulging azure eyes. When he sits on his veranda in the evening, he is often seen smoking his pipe.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c6 P56](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0056)_

## Personality

Pettifer is a peculiar, candid, and impetuous man who prides himself on speaking his mind directly regardless of how blunt it may sound. Though he can be short-tempered and exacting when reviewing work, he is also pleasant, supportive, and capable of being a friendly neighbor. He resents being an object of pity and historically harbored a strong bias against matrimony.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c17 P76](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0076), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v2 c27 P9](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0009), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P72](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0072)_

## History

After relocating from Scottsford, New Brunswick to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer purchased the western neighboring farm of the Abernethy place. He lived for a time as a bachelor with irregular household routines, employing young John Henry Carter to assist him. An early incident involving a stray cow brought him into direct acquaintance with Nell Abernethy, with whom he quickly formed a firm friendship. Though rumor once suggested he was courting Isabella Pullen when he was actually visiting Mr. Gorham Pullen for business and playing checkers with Mr. Pettifer Pullen, he eventually married Emily Scott in fulfillment of a promise made to his late sister. Following his marriage, he adjusted to his wife's compulsive housecleaning and social ties, though he maintained an armed neutrality toward Agatha Sowerby. In addition to his farm duties and delivering mail, he offered literary critiques and support to Nell when she began writing stories.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c17 P76](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0076), [v2 c24 P5](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c30 P5](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0005), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024)_

## Background by volume

- lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick before moving to Brierley  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- routinely flogged by his schoolmaster as a boy  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>
- received his parrot Nutmeg from his brother, a seafaring man  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## Quotes

> Ignore that parrot. He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily.  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

> Tut, tut, miss, do not utter a single further word regarding it. It is immaterial . . . utterly immaterial. Misfortunes are bound to occur. On occasion, I am overly impetuous myself, miss . . . much too impetuous. However, I am unable to refrain from voicing my exact thoughts, and people are required to accept me as I am. Now, had that cow gotten into my cabbages . . . yet do not dwell on it, she did not, hence everything is fine. Because you wish to dispose of her, I believe I would prefer taking your cow in trade.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> Back when I attended school, the master flogged me routinely each day on the grounds that if I was not causing trouble at that moment, I was planning it.  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>

> That old bother Agatha Sowerby dropped by once more today, nagging me to contribute money for purchasing a vestry room carpet. My hatred for that woman exceeds my feelings for anyone else I am acquainted with. In merely six words, she is capable of compressing an entire sermon—complete with text, commentary, and application—and launching it at your head as if it were a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> I do not believe in delaying marriage for too long—as I did.  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
